data.revised_prompt: The quadcopter in <Picture 1> is <Subject 1>. The dark grey studio background and overhead lighting setup in <Picture 1> are <Subject 2>. The spatial layout of the four red dots and intersecting blue lines in <Picture 2> is <Subject 3>. The target image shows <Subject 1> against <Subject 2>, redrawn so that its four motor hubs and arms align with the geometry of <Subject 3> without rendering the red dots or blue lines themselves. <Subject 1> is partially preserved; its streamlined fuselage, materials, cold grey color scheme, blue LED light band, carbon fiber frame, ABS propellers, and top-view orientation remain, while the positions and angles of its four foldable arms and motor hubs change to match <Subject 3>. <Subject 2> is fully preserved. <Subject 3> supplies the exact motor hub positions and arm alignment transferred to <Subject 1>. The four motor hubs of <Subject 1> are positioned at the exact coordinates of the four red dots in <Subject 3>, forming a wide X-shaped layout with a 52-degree rotor angle and a 1.3-to-1 arm span ratio. The four articulated arms of <Subject 1> extend along the paths of the blue lines in <Subject 3>, connecting seamlessly from the central fuselage to the repositioned reinforced motor covers and two-blade propellers. The cast shadows on <Subject 2> beneath the arms and rotors adjust accordingly to match the new wider, shallower diagonal span.
